title: Spreading your money
blurb: Why one failure hurts less when money is spread out, and what spreading cannot fix.
t1.title: Many baskets
t1.hook: Asha has {total} and six mini-businesses to choose from. They are a farm, a tea stall, a repair shop, a cloth shop, a bus and a tech start-up. Heavy rain hits the farm. Your mission: see how splitting helps.
t1.define: **Diversification** means spreading money across different things, so one failure hurts less.
t1.analogy: Carry all your eggs in one basket and one trip breaks them all. Spread them over several baskets, and one fall breaks only a few.
q1.opt.b: Putting everything in the best thing
q1.hint: Think of the eggs and the baskets.
q1.explain: Diversification is spreading money across different things.
q2.prompt: Asha puts all {total} into the farm. What is the main danger?
q2.opt.a: If the farm does badly, her whole amount takes the hit
q2.opt.c: She will pay no tax on it
q2.hint: Where is all of her money sitting?
q2.explain: With everything in one place, a bad result there hits her whole amount.
t2.title: Try the split
t2.define: Let us test it. Hold your {total} in equal slices and let one business fall. Then change how many businesses share the money.
t2.explore: Open the lab. Set the fall to {fall}. Choose how many businesses share your {total}, with "One business falls" selected.
q3.prompt: In the lab, hold just 1 business and set the fall to {fall}. What is your loss? Type a number in rupees.
q3.hint: Your whole amount sits in the business that fell.
q3.explain: All {total} is in it, and it falls {fall}. The loss is {lossOne}.
q4.prompt: Now split across all 6 businesses, with one falling {fall}. What is your loss? Type a number in rupees.
q4.hint: Only one slice sits in the business that fell.
q4.explain: Each business holds {each}. Only that slice falls {fall}, so the loss is {lossSplit}.
q5.prompt: Why is the loss smaller when you split?
q5.opt.a: Only a small slice sits in the business that fell
q5.opt.b: The business that fell recovers faster
q5.opt.c: Fees are lower with more businesses
q5.fb.d: Spreading lowers the damage from one failure. It does not remove risk, as the next task shows.
q5.hint: Compare how much money sits in the business that fell.
q5.explain: A small slice in the business that fell means a small loss.
t3.title: What spreading cannot do
t3.define: Spreading helps when **one** thing goes wrong. It cannot help much when a fall hits **everything** at once, like a market-wide scare.
t3.explore: Open the lab again. Pick "The whole market falls" and set the fall to {fall}. Try different splits.
q6.prompt: In the lab, let the whole market fall {fall} and split across all 6 businesses. What is your loss? Type a number in rupees.
q6.hint: When everything falls, every slice falls.
q6.explain: Every slice falls {fall}, so the loss is {lossMarket}, whether you hold one business or six.
q7.prompt: Asha now holds all six businesses. Which statement is correct?
q7.opt.a: She can still lose money, for example if everything falls together
q7.opt.b: She cannot lose money any more
q7.opt.c: She will earn more than anyone with one business
q7.fb.b: Spreading lowers the damage from one failure. A fall that hits everything still costs her.
q7.fb.c: Nobody can promise that. Spreading can lower the swings, but it does not guarantee more profit.
q7.hint: Remember what happened when the whole market fell.
q7.explain: Spreading lowers the risk from one failure. It cannot remove a fall that hits everything.
t4.title: The Mixed Basket
t4.define: The **Mixed Basket** path holds many different things in one. Its average growth is a little lower than the Bumpy Ride's. Its swings are much smaller.
t4.explore: Open the lab. Compare the Mixed Basket and the Bumpy Ride for {amt}.
q8.prompt: Pick the Mixed Basket with {amt}. How many rupees wide is its typical-year range? Type a number in rupees.
q8.explain: The range runs from {mLow} to {mHigh}. It is {mWidth} wide.
q9.prompt: How many rupees narrower is the Mixed Basket's range than the Bumpy Ride's? Type a number in rupees.
q9.hint: Find both widths in the lab and subtract.
q9.explain: The Bumpy Ride's range is {bWidth} wide and the Mixed Basket's is {mWidth}. The gap is {narrower}.
q10.prompt: Why is the Mixed Basket's range narrower?
q10.opt.a: Its money is spread over many things, which smooths the swings
q10.opt.b: It holds fewer things than the Bumpy Ride
q10.opt.c: It is guaranteed not to fall
q10.fb.c: No path is guaranteed. The Mixed Basket still has bad years. Its range is just narrower.
q10.hint: Think about the six businesses and the one that fell.
q10.explain: Spreading over many things smooths the swings. That is why the range is narrower.
t5.title: Not too many
t5.define: More is not always better. Holding 40 things you do not understand is not the goal. Know what you hold, and watch the costs.
t5.tradeoff: Spreading lowers the damage from one failure. It also lowers the chance of one big winner. It is a trade-off.
q11.prompt: A friend says one hot company is all anyone needs. What is the problem?
q11.opt.a: If that one company fails, your whole amount is hit
q11.opt.b: One hot company is enough, so there is no problem
q11.opt.c: A single company can never rise
q11.fb.b: One company can fall or fail, and then your whole amount takes the hit.
q11.hint: Think of the farm, with all the money in it.
q11.explain: A single company can fail, and with all the money in it, you take the whole hit.
q12.prompt: Which sentence about spreading money is true?
q12.opt.a: It lowers the damage from one failure but cannot remove all risk
q12.opt.b: More items always means better results
q12.opt.d: It means never checking what you hold
q12.fb.c: Nothing guarantees a profit. Spreading only lowers the damage from one failure.
q12.hint: Remember both what spreading can do and what it cannot.
q12.explain: Spreading helps with one failure. It cannot remove every risk, and it guarantees nothing.
glossary.diversification.def: Spreading money across different things so one failure hurts less.
glossary.market_wide_fall.def: A fall that hits almost everything at once.
